extracted.intended_audience: Jane Coffin Childs Fellows, their sponsoring institutions and postdoctoral advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Terms and conditions governing a three-year Jane Coffin Childs postdoctoral fellowship, including stipend, allowances, reporting, benefits, intellectual property, and communication requirements for fellows and their sponsoring institutions/advisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of Fellowship (length)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment will be for three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships are structured as three-year appointments. Any deviations in term length would require Fund approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing laboratory or postdoctoral advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes of laboratory and postdoctoral advisor during the course of the fellowship require the permission of the Director with the advice of the Board of Scientific Advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund recognizes valid reasons for such changes but requires advance approval; contact the Director and the Board of Scientific Advisors for permission before making changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to mentoring and diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: The JCC Fund is committed to mentoring and advancing people from all backgrounds and is dedicated to increasing the diversity of the scientific workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of program values; implies that the Fund considers diversity and mentoring as part of its mission when administering awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance at annual symposium
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance at the annual symposium of the Jane Coffin Childs Fund is required each year of the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All meeting expenses for attendees’ travel, lodging, and JCC-hosted meals are paid by JCC. Fellows must plan to attend yearly symposia as a condition of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status of award (employment relationship)
rubrics_metrics.description: An award does not constitute an employer-employee relationship between the Foundation and the JCC Fellow, if supported by JCC or Merck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship is a funding award, not an employment contract; fellows and institutions should treat it accordingly for administrative and legal purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical benefits requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: During the term of the fellowship, postdoctoral advisors are required to provide medical benefits for the Fellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sponsoring advisor/institution must ensure the fellow has medical benefits for the duration of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special terms for JCC/HHMI partnership fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: JCC Fellows supported by the JCC/HHMI partnership and in the laboratory of an HHMI investigator have unique terms as outlined at the time of the award by JCC and HHMI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows in this partnership should follow the specific, potentially different terms provided at award; consult JCC and HHMI documentation provided with the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend amounts by year
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic stipend is $72,000 for the first year, $74,000 for the second year, and $76,000 the third year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipend is specified per fellowship year; institutions should budget and disburse according to these amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent child stipend
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional $1,000 of stipend support is provided annually per dependent child under the age of 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows with eligible dependents receive this supplement each year; subject to Fund rules regarding dependent eligibility (under 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory research allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: An allowance of $2,000 a year will be made available to the laboratory sponsoring the fellow for research costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research allowance is intended for research costs (not travel). Use is left to the discretion of the fellow and proposed postdoctoral advisor. Research funds may be carried over with approval from the program office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on research allowance use
rubrics_metrics.description: The research allowance is not to be used for travel and the use of the research funds is left to the discrepancy of the fellow and proposed postdoctoral advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the $2,000/year research allowance for travel. The Fund expects the fellow and advisor to agree on appropriate research expenditures; carryover requires program office approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel allowance for meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: An allowance of $1,800 total will be provided at the onset of the award for travel to scientific meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel funding is to be spent over the three-year fellowship and is managed by the Fellows’ institution. The $1,800 is a total amount (not annual).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joan A. Steitz Fund childcare stipends
rubrics_metrics.description: The Joan A. Steitz Fund was established to provide stipends for child care to all fellows with dependents under the age of 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no application or paperwork due from the fellow; further information will be provided to awardees at the time of award. This is an additional childcare support mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency for second and third year funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Second and third year funding of awards is contingent upon submission of an annual fiscal and narrative report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows must submit required fiscal and narrative reports annually to receive continued funding beyond year one; failure to submit may jeopardize continued support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No indirect costs are provided to the sponsoring institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund awards are for full-time postdoctoral training and do not include overhead/indirect cost reimbursement to institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows should notify the Fund whenever a patent has been applied for and Jane Coffin Childs Fund has supported the awardee during the development of the patentable intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification is required when patent applications relate to work supported by the Fund so the Fund is informed of IP stemming from supported research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to institutional patent policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Jane Coffin Childs Fund requests that awardees adhere to the established patent policy of the institution at which the primary postdoctoral advisor is working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows should follow their institution's patent policies regarding ownership, disclosure, and commercialization of inventions developed during the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication communication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellow should communicate new publication details during the tenure of their fellowship to the JCC Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows must inform the JCC Office about new publications produced during the fellowship period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding acknowledgement wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows should acknowledge support from the Fund by including the following statement: (FELLOW’S NAME) is a Fellow of The Jane Coffin Childs Fund for Medical Research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact acknowledgement wording in publications and other appropriate outputs produced during the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo use and funder designation on presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: If presenting a poster or talk, fellows should include the Jane Coffin Childs Fund logo to their materials and designate Jane Coffin Childs Fund as a funder in all funding acknowledgements during your tenure as a fellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the Fund's logo on posters/talks and list JCC as a funder in funding acknowledgements while the fellowship is active.
